en.headline: Only 3% of Hong Kong firms fully integrate AI into workflows, survey finds
en.dek: Accenture polled 150 companies and released results on Wednesday, finding strong interest but hurdles including resistance to change and outdated infrastructure.
body: Consultancy Accenture said only 3 per cent of Hong Kong companies have fully integrated artificial intelligence into their workflows, according to a survey of 150 firms whose results were released on Wednesday.

The poll indicated that businesses showed a strong desire to adopt AI but many struggled to put it into practice. Robert Hah, the consultancy’s Hong Kong office lead, said Hong Kong had strong AI ambitions and the right ingredients in place, yet few enterprises had scaled AI across the business.

Respondents expected AI to raise productivity by an average of 15 per cent and cut costs by 11 per cent over an 18-month period, the survey found. Hah pointed to government initiatives to promote the industry and upskill the workforce, as well as Hong Kong’s capital markets, as favourable conditions.

zh.headline: 調查指僅3%港企將人工智能全面融入工作流程
zh.dek: 埃森哲周三公布對150家企業的調查結果，指企業有強烈採用意欲，但面臨組織變革阻力及數碼基建過時等障礙。
body: 顧問公司埃森哲表示，一項對150家企業的調查顯示，只有3%的香港公司已將人工智能全面融入其工作流程，結果於周三公布。
調查指出，企業對採用人工智能有強烈意欲，但許多在實踐上遇到困難。埃森哲香港辦公室負責人Robert Hah表示，香港有強烈的人工智能野心及合適條件，但很少企業能將人工智能擴展至整個業務。
受訪者預期人工智能可在18個月內平均提升生產力15%及降低成本11%。Hah指政府推動產業及提升勞動力技能的措施，以及香港的資本市場，都是有利條件。
